Working entry (`chk-7bdqpplh`, Epoch 6 — The fleet console, viola-0.2.0): «Console actions — every verb by keyboard
alone, no key trap, through the CLI verbs; a send shows its readback; refusals as `unable` lines».

- `viola console` gains ACTIONS over the view the fleet-console-view chunk built: a selection of one row of the board,
  and the verbs reached from that selection by keyboard alone.

- Each action acts through the CLI verb it names ("through the CLI verbs"): the same outcome and the same refusal as
  the verb typed at a shell, with no second code path for an action (matrix#v2-15's requirement).
- A send shows its readback: the frame verb's own reply, never the view's STATUS cell (carry cry-qjw64paz).
- A refusal of an action shows as the verb's `unable` line on the console's own surface.
- No key trap: every mode the actions add is left by keyboard alone.

- A key decoder of key SEQUENCES, replacing the scaffold's one-class-per-read decoder where the actions need it
  (carry cry-pjtbjcco).
- Nothing of the view's content changes beyond what a selection and an action's result need (directive item 1).

- Which verbs the console offers in THIS entry, their keys, the selection model, the send's text entry, any confirm,
  any scroll, and whether the entry splits, are open forks of the operator's (directive item 3); the scope names them
  as forks, never as built.

- No live reading is made by this chunk's first pass: a capability clause that needs one is claimed GATED, its
  reading the operator's to grant and to time (directive item 1).

- The gated chunk `2026-11-28-fleet-console-view` stays gated: its premise (the operator's live reading of the view at
  his host) is untouched here.

- CARRY cry-mf2w3ioc (from «Switching a session's model and effort», PROVISIONAL, a delegate's placement): v2-31's
  console leg — the switch reached by keyboard alone; `viola switch` is CLI-only (fork F5, a delegate's word,
  PROVISIONAL), so the console reaches it through the CLI verb.

- CARRY cry-pjtbjcco (from «Console scaffold», PROVISIONAL): the scaffold's key decoder reads ONE class per read of at
  most 64 bytes — 0x03 anywhere interrupt, exactly `q` quit, anything else one `unbound` — so the actions need a
  decoder of key sequences; its restore case proves the line mode raw while the frame stands and cooked after the
  quit, read on the console's own terminal, never that the mode after equals the mode before

# Phase directive — «Console actions» (Epoch 6 — The fleet console, viola-0.2.0; the head entry `chk-7bdqpplh` at `a07542e9`)

**WHAT IS AN INPUT, AND WHAT IS NOT.** Of the folder this directive stands in, the ONLY files you read or snap are
this directive and the relay files a later send names. A fact the plan needs and this directive does not state is
ASKED of the overseer in the P3 block, never looked up.

**The operator is AWAY, reached only through the overseer**: raise NO question dialog for him. A fork that is his
is written to `{run_dir}/founder-forks.md` (the question, the options in order with each one's cost, the
recommendation marked); his answer comes later through the overseer. **A boundary widening or a product choice is
never built on a delegate's word:** where the entry needs one, the P3 block names it, and the phase STOPS at the
P3 block's end saying so in one line — it does not go on to a P5 card that would only be held. A technical fork
is answered by the overseer's relay at once. **This phase makes NO live start, opens, moves, focuses or closes NO
window on the operator's desktop, dispatches nothing to the compositor (a read-only query of its help, version or
state is allowed; say each one you ran), sends no key to a real terminal, runs no real `claude` in any form and no
live arm of any `scripts/r*.sh`, runs no mutation run, sends nothing to any real instance, and reads nothing of
the operator's real `~/.claude*` or `~/.viola` — a `viola list` or a `viola console` there among them.** In your
chat messages name a compiled screen literal, never print it. Every time you write comes from `date -u`, read at
the moment of writing.

## Facts, measured by the overseer at 2026-11-28T13:42:34Z — cite them as this directive's

- The tree at `a07542e9` = its upstream, ci#46149816293 green 7 of 7; two tracked bookkeeping paths dirty; 142

  the CLI verbs; a send shows its readback; refusals as `unable` lines». It carries three carries — v2-31's
  console leg (the switch by keyboard, through the CLI verb), the scaffold's key decoder and restore reading
  (one class per read of at most 64 bytes: `q`, Ctrl-C, everything else «unbound»; the restore proven raw-while-

  board's order then `... <n> more`; the board re-read once a second, the agents read at most every 5 s; `LAST`

  offers, their keys, how a row is selected, how text for a send is typed, what a confirm is — each is unanswered.

  against `python3 ~/dev/projects/additional/andromedaV3/andromeda-overseer/docs/tools/hostwatch.py read --from
  <UTC> --to <UTC>` first and never re-run for green; read `df -m /tmp` beside it.

## The directive

1. Scope is the route entry and its three carries as they stand at `a07542e9` — the ACTIONS: nothing of the view's
   content changes beyond what a selection and an action's result need. Say at P1, clause by clause of the head

   this entry builds, which clauses the fakes and the keystroke driver's state reads prove, and which need a live

   and to time, never fired by this chunk's first pass.

   fixtures:** the full list of CLI verbs with, for each, what it needs (a name, a text, a pair, a workspace, a
   confirmation) and whether it can be reached «through the CLI verbs» from inside the console without a second
   process (which functions the verbs' own code exposes; what running the verb as a child would cost and write);
   what a send's readback is today, by its row and its code, and how long it can take against the one-second
   read; every refusal each verb can print as an `unable` line, by its census; what «no key trap» asks by its
   a11y rows; what the key decoder must read for the keys the options below need (arrows and escape sequences
   split across reads, a paste, a resize arriving mid-sequence) and how the driver feeds and reads each — state,
   never the screen; what a text entry for a send needs (an editing line, a paste, a multi-line text, a bound) and
   what of it exists.
3. **Forks, each with its options priced and marked his or technical.** His, at the least: WHICH verbs the console
   offers in this entry (all of them, or a named first set with the rest a later entry); the KEY for each and the
   way a row is selected (and what happens to the selection when the fleet changes under it); how the text of a
   send is entered; whether a destructive or wheel-moving verb asks a confirm and in what words; any row the
   actions must narrow, except or reword (name each; the conservative arm is a NAMED exception, never a
   generalised rule); whether the view scrolls to reach a hidden row; whether one implement window holds the
   entry, and if not the split — «every verb by keyboard» may be two or three entries, and a split is his.
   Technical, the overseer's: the decoder's shape, the state-read events, module layout, the test homes.
4. Read the playbook's escalate rows BEFORE the P3 block is written. Search ALL seven masters by the counted
   literals a row or a test pins (the verbs' list and count, the keys' rows, the console's surface rows, the
   refusal census, the wheel rows, the send rows and their bounds) and by «never», «only»; name every reached row
   with the read-not-reached beside it, and say of each «not reached» reading which row it rests on.
5. **At P3's END:** ONE block in `founder-forks.md` — your window, the measurements, every reached row, each fork
   of his with its options priced and a recommendation. If NO fork of his is a boundary widening or a product
   choice the build stands on, go on to P4; otherwise STOP there with one line.
6. A step that asserts what existing code does cites the symbol and line it read. Every `gate.py control` has an
   id of 1–16 characters, its `--timeout S`, and an entry filtered to its guard's own cases. Every filter term
   SELECTS at least one test under its layer flag once its step is built and none on the untouched tree. An
   expect atom must be able to fail — an entry that reads a record reads red on an empty one; when a new event or
   field joins a schema, the plan names EVERY list and schema that pins it. A loop or a thread the plan adds
   states its log volume per hour at a 33-instance fleet and what bounds it. A test that drives the console runs
   under a test-owned home, its own pseudo-terminal and the test-scoped `PATH`, takes a bound under the 20 s lint,
   reads state and never the screen, and sends to fake-agent instances only.
7. A guard's or the permission classifier's refusal is never routed around: stop and tell the overseer. Call NO
   scheduled-wake or timer tool. End every process you start; remove no scratch clone by a recursive delete —
   name it on the card. Scripted edits are followed by the formatter. Leaves hold no figure the code states.
8. Run the phase exactly as the letters say, read as they stand. On the P5 card, in one block, verbatim where a
   tool printed it: the union's per-master lines and the `rows-union` line; whether EVERY cited row is in the
   union or its standing list; planlint's own lines whole; the claim's lines for any capability claimed and its

# Relay — the operator's answers to the forks of «Console actions» (chunk 2026-11-28-console-actions, phase run 2026-11-28T13-46-51Z-phase)

**The operator's OWN answers**, given by two question dialogs (read at 2026-11-28T14:32:05Z and 14:35:31Z), each
option shown as `founder-forks.md` priced it. Each is his word, not a delegate's: nothing of it rests PROVISIONAL.

- **F1 — «Дочерний, как человек (Recommended)»**: a direct child `viola` per action, its own exe, `--home` passed,
  `VIOLA_NAME` / `VIOLA_DIR` removed from its env so the console acts as the HUMAN, output captured and drawn
  escaped, one child at a time. He was told it is a boundary widening (a new subprocess crossing, about six rows
  reworded, a child may still run at a quit).
- **F2 and F7, put to him as ONE question — «Всё одним чанком»**: AGAINST the recommended split. ALL EIGHT verbs
  of v2-15 (open, focus, send, answer, last, pause, release, revive) PLUS switch, in THIS entry, ONE entry. He was
  shown the price: about twice the work, past one implement window, a risk of a stopped implement and a revision.
  No «Console send and switch» entry is inserted; v2-15 is this entry's to build whole.
- **F3 — «Стрелки/jk + буквы (Recommended)»**: Up/Down and `j`/`k` over the wrapped rows in the board's order; one
  lower-case letter per verb (`s` send · `l` last · `p` pause · `r` release · `f` focus · `v` revive · `m`
  switch); `q` / Ctrl-C quit from the list; the selection stays on the same NAME when the fleet changes, else the
  nearest row in order.
- **F4 — «Одна строка (Recommended)»**: one editing line on the key row, Enter sends, Esc cancels, the text
  unchanged to `viola send`; one line per send.
- **F5 — «Только release и revive (Recommended)»**: a one-key `y/n` confirm for release and revive ONLY; every
  other action acts at once.
- **F6 — «Следует за выбором (Recommended)»**: the body follows the selection; `... <n> above` beside
  `... <n> more`.

## What his «всё одним чанком» leaves — the overseer's TECHNICAL word

1. **Letters for the three verbs his F3 option did not show:** `a` answer · `o` open a child · `d` adopt.
   Collision-free against `s l p r f v m q j k`. If the code shows a clash (a key the decoder already owns), say
   so and take the next free mnemonic, named on the card.
2. **ONE entry, TWO implement windows, planned so — no route change.** The plan is written in two ordered parts
   with a planned stop between them, each closed by its own green crate layers and a state on disk:
   - **Part 1:** the sequence decoder, the selection, the scroll (F6), the child runner (F1), the confirm (F5),
     and the five verbs that need no new input — last, pause, release, focus, revive (as `viola up <name>`).

`viola console` gains its actions. The human selects one wrapped row of the board by keyboard and runs each of
matrix#v2-15's eight verbs, plus `viola switch` (v2-31's console leg), on it. Each action runs the CLI verb itself as a
direct child process of the console's own exe, with `--home` passed and `VIOLA_NAME` / `VIOLA_DIR` removed so the
console acts as the human (F1). Its stdout and stderr are captured through `MAX_FRAME` and drawn escaped on the
console's own surface. So the outcome and the refusal are the verb's own, with no second code path for an action
(research §Patterns: a verb owns its process's subscriber and streams, `src/cmd/client.rs:44-47`,
`src/cmd/send.rs:100-169`).

One child runs at a time, on its own thread; the key loop stays live, because a send can take up to 53.5 s
(`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/screen.rs:16-31`). A byte-level decoder reads key sequences, with a 50 ms lone-ESC
wait. The selection follows the board's order and survives a fleet change (F3), and the body scrolls with it (F6).
release and revive ask `y`/`n` (F5). A send takes one editing line (F4). Every action writes one closed
`console-action` line, holding the verb word and the exit code, never a name or a text. Per security-plan
`decision/console-key-reader-bounded` and obs-plan `decision/codes-only-role-logs`.

title: Part 1 — the decoder, the selection, the scroll, the runner, the confirm and five verbs

data.head: ### Part 1 — the decoder, the selection, the scroll, the runner, the confirm and five verbs

body:
2. **The selection and the scroll** (`src/console/view.rs`, `src/human/fleet.rs`). The view takes a selection, the
   board item's name (never the drawn text, carry cry-qjw64paz), over the wrapped rows in the board's forest order;
   unwrapped rows are never selected (F3). Up and down move it, clamped at the ends. On a fleet change it keeps its
   name; if the name is gone, it takes the row now at the old position, clamped. On an empty or all-unwrapped board,
   no selection. The selected row is drawn with `> ` before it and every other body row with two spaces (ASCII,
   design S1). The body window follows the selection (F6): rows hidden above end in one `... <n> above` line at the
   body's top, and rows below in the standing `... <n> more`. `View::shown` / `hidden` count both. Cases named
   `selection_…` and `scroll_…`.

3. **The action runner** (`src/console/action.rs`, new; wired in `src/console/mod.rs`). An `Action` is a verb word
   of a closed enum and its argv after the verb, plus an optional stdin text. `run` spawns
   `<exe> --home <home> <verb> <name> …` directly, with no shell (arch `decision/no-shell-out`):
   - `<exe>` is the console's own canonical exe and `<home>` its canonical home, both read once at start in
     `src/cmd/console.rs` (precedent `src/cmd/plugin.rs:108`);
   - its env is the console's, with `VIOLA_NAME` and `VIOLA_DIR` removed (F1);
   - its cwd is the console's;
   - stdin is null, or a pipe the text is written to and closed;
   - stdout and stderr are piped, each read on its own thread through `take(MAX_FRAME)` ahead of the read call (the
     census form, security.md 2026-11-16).
   It is not tied to the console's death: a child running at a quit runs to its verb's own end, and its output is
   dropped (F1, as he was told). The result is the exit code and the captured lines, split on LF. Each line is
   escaped through the board's row escape before it is drawn (design-system `decision/escape-controls-in-human-output`).
   `run` returns on its own thread through a channel; the loop takes one action at a time, and an action key while one
   runs is read `busy` and runs nothing. Cases named `action_…`.

4. **The loop's modes** (`src/console/mod.rs`, `run`, lines 148-206). The loop keeps a mode:
   - **list:** up, down, a verb letter, quit, interrupt;
   - **confirm:** `y` runs, `n` or escape cancels, interrupt ends the console, anything else unbound;
   - **editing:** Part 2.
   `recv_timeout` takes the nearer of `POLL` and the decoder's ESC deadline. Every mode is left by one key and Ctrl-C
   ends the console from every mode (no key trap). Each key writes one `console-key` line whose word is its meaning in
   its mode (step 7). A finished child writes one `console-action` line and sets the result view.

5. **The result view and the key line** (`src/human/console.rs`, `src/console/view.rs`). While an action runs, the
   body's last row reads `<verb>  <name>  running`. Once it ends, the action's lines take the body's lower rows, at
   most a third of the body, with the cut rule and `... <n> more` past them. An escape or the next action clears them.
   The key line keeps `q quit` first, so a cut never hides it, then the bindings in order:
   `q quit  jk move  l last  p pause  r release  f focus  v revive` (Part 2 appends `s send  m switch  a answer  o open`).
   A confirm or editing mode replaces the key line with its prompt.

7. **The `console-action` event and the key words.**
   - `crates/viola-core/src/obs.rs`: `ObsEvent::ConsoleAction`, `console-action`, in `ALL`, its `Display` and the
     pinned `LOG_FORMAT_EVENTS` (lines 37-56, 170-194).
   - `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`: the event enum, a message arm and a field arm with `verb` (enum `last` · `pause` ·
     `release` · `focus` · `up` · `send` · `switch` · `answer` · `open`) and `exit_code` (integer), both required. The
     `console-key` arm's `key` enum grows to `quit` · `interrupt` · `unbound` · `up` · `down` · `action` · `busy` ·
     `yes` · `no` · `escape` · `enter` · `backspace` · `text` (`text` and `enter` written in Part 2).
   - `schemas/diag-detail.v1.json`: the event enum.
   - `tests/contract_diag_schema.rs`: `LOG_FORMAT_EVENTS` (line 36).
   - The obs-plan and test-plan rows go to the wrap (Implementation notes).
   No line carries a name, an argument, a text or a child's output (keeps obs S4, tests S7).

8. **The start's handover** (`src/cmd/console.rs`). Read the canonical exe and the canonical home once, before
   `console::run`, and pass them in `Sources`. The start's checks stay first and unchanged (security-plan
   `decision/console-terminal-and-home-check`).

9. **Part 1's E2E cases** (`tests/tui_console.rs`, `tests/support/`). Every case meets these:
   - an outer PTY, a test-owned home, a test-owned HOME and the test-scoped PATH, with the fake agent as `claude` and
     the fake foot and hyprctl first on the PATH;
   - fake-agent instances only, the tied builder, and waits on lines (keeps tests S1, S2, S6; security S1; obs S2, S3);
   - verdicts read from `console.ndjson`, the instance's `events.ndjson` and the console tty's line mode, never the
     screen.
   The cases:
   - `console_selection_moves_over_wrapped_rows_and_skips_unwrapped`
   - `console_selection_keeps_its_name_when_the_fleet_changes`
   - `console_scroll_follows_the_selection`
   - `console_pause_runs_the_verb_as_a_child_like_a_shell` — the console's pause writes the same wheel record, and a
     `console-action{verb:pause, exit_code}` equal to the exit of `viola pause` run at a shell on a twin instance
   - `console_release_asks_then_runs_on_yes`
   - `console_release_confirm_left_by_escape_runs_nothing`
   - `console_last_draws_the_verbs_reply`
   - `console_focus_runs_the_verb_over_the_fake_compositor`
   - `console_revive_asks_then_runs_up_on_yes` — the fake foot's spawn record names `revive <name> --origin`;
     teardown through the shared stand-in teardown
   - `console_refused_action_logs_the_verbs_exit_code` — pause on a dead instance gives exit 21
   - `console_ctrl_c_ends_from_every_mode` — list and confirm in Part 1; restored, exit 0

   The schema check covers every line (obs S1). Fixed copy is pinned by literal: the confirm prompts, the running
   line and the key line (a11y S3, tests S4).

**Part 1's end:** the tree holds steps 1–9, every entry of the block marked part 1 green, and the whole unit,
integration and e2e layers green. No Part-2 key is bound: `s` `m` `a` `o` read `unbound`.

title: Part 2 — the editing line, send, switch, open and answer (begins on Q8 and Q9's answers)

data.head: ### Part 2 — the editing line, send, switch, open and answer (begins on Q8 and Q9's answers)

body:
11. **send** — `s`, the prompt `send <name>: `, enter → `viola send <name>` with the line on its stdin. Its mirror
    lines (`[RB] read back` · `[  ] unconfirmable` · `[/ ] unable …` and its hint) are its readback, drawn as captured
    (carry cry-qjw64paz: never STATUS). An empty line is the verb's own `empty-text` refusal, exit 13.

12. **switch** — `m`, the prompt `switch <name>: `. Each space-separated word that is one of the five effort words
    becomes `--effort <word>`; any other word becomes `--model <word>`. Enter → `viola switch <name> …`, and its line
    or refusal is drawn, exit 2 on a bad word included.

13. **open a child** — `o`, the prompt `open child of <name>: `, enter →
    `viola open <typed> --parent <name> -- claude`; its line or refusal is drawn.

14. **answer — HELD behind Q8.** Built only once Q8's answer is snapped. On arm 2 (recommended): `a` on a row whose
    dialog is a permission or a plan asks `allow <name>? y/n` or `approve <name>? y/n`. `y` / `n` runs
    `viola answer <name> <dialog_id>` with the closed response JSON on stdin (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/dialog.rs:220-255`).
    The dialog id comes from the snapshot through a board field kept out of `list --json`
    (`crates/viola-state/src/board.rs:375-384`). On a question, `a` draws `<name>  question - answer it in the session (f)`.
    Arm 1 or arm 3 is a revision of this step, never improvised.

15. **Part 2's cases** — units `decoder_editing_…`, `action_send_…`, `action_switch_…`, `action_open_…`; and in
    `tests/tui_console.rs`:
    - `console_send_hands_the_line_to_the_verb_and_logs_its_exit` — the events log holds the verb's `send-issued`
      and `prompt-submitted`, and `console-action{verb:send, exit_code:0}`
    - `console_send_empty_line_is_the_verbs_refusal` — exit 13
    - `console_editing_line_left_by_escape_runs_nothing`
    - `console_switch_hands_its_words_to_the_verb` — the fake agent's start receipt carries the pair
    - `console_open_hands_the_name_and_parent_to_the_verb` — the fake foot's spawn record
    - `console_answer_permission_by_y` (on Q8 arm 1 or 2)

    `console_ctrl_c_ends_from_every_mode` gains the editing mode.
- `src/console/action.rs` — the action table, the child spawn, the captured result
- `src/console/keys.rs` — the sequence decoder in place of `Key::of`
- `src/console/mod.rs` — the modes, the selection, the runner's channel, the ESC deadline
- `src/console/view.rs` — the selection mark, the scroll, the above line, the result rows
- `src/human/console.rs` — the key line, the prompts, the running line
- `src/human/fleet.rs` — the selection gutter on the body lines
- `src/cmd/console.rs` — the exe and home handed to the loop
- `crates/viola-core/src/obs.rs` — `ObsEvent::ConsoleAction`
- `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` — the console-action arms and the console-key words
- `schemas/diag-detail.v1.json` — the event enum
- `tests/contract_diag_schema.rs` — the pinned event list
- `tests/tui_console.rs` — the action cases
- `crates/viola-state/src/board.rs` — Part 2 step 14 only, held on Q8: the dialog id on the item, kept out of `list --json`

The block runs, in order: the formatter and the linter; the core crate's units; the root binaries' units and the new
unit cases of each part (0 on the untouched tree); the console binary whole and each part's new cases (0 on the
untouched tree); the contract binaries the event touches; the schema arm; the host read; the harness's unit,
integration and e2e layers; then the operator pass. Each entry's `note` names its part.

**What is not run, and why:** no round, no live entry, no live start, no real `claude`, no compositor call and no
mutation run (inputs#I1). **Boot path:** test-plan declares no boot-path list. By shape, `src/main.rs`, the run start
and the board read under `viola list` are untouched in Part 1, so no smoke entry stands. Part 2's step 14 touches
`crates/viola-state/src/board.rs`; there, `binary(cli_list) | binary(cross_list_rows)` stands as Part 2's entry. No
dependency moves, so `cargo deny check` stands as CI's job.

**The remove-the-guard controls** are implement's one-shot `gate.py control` runs, never entries. Each runs on its
filtered entry below with `--timeout 900`, a clone build of the root crate and one case. Each case fails on its own
assertion with no wait, so a `timeout` reading would NOT read the guard as held.

  `action_child_env_drops_the_instance_names` and `contract_bounded_readers` green (F1, inputs#I2; arch
  `decision/no-shell-out`).

- (product) From a selected wrapped row, by keyboard alone, `l` `p` `f` run last, pause and focus, and `r`·`y` and
  `v`·`y` run release and `up <name>`. Each gives the verb's own record and exit, equal to the shell verb's, and one
  `console-action{verb, exit_code}` line: the part-1 e2e filter green (matrix#v2-15, its Part-1 legs).

  Ctrl-C ends the console from every mode, exit 0 and the line mode cooked after (test-plan
  `decision/console-restore-read-on-own-terminal`): `console_ctrl_c_ends_from_every_mode` and
  `console_release_confirm_left_by_escape_runs_nothing` green.

  key byte to any line: the part-1 unit filter green (security-plan `decision/console-key-reader-bounded`).

body:
**Chunk:** the fleet console's actions — every verb by keyboard from a selected row, through the CLI verbs, a send's readback, refusals as `unable` lines (Part 1 of 2: the decoder, the selection, the scroll, the runner, the confirm and five verbs)
**Date:** 2026-11-28
**Run:** 2026-11-28T14-52-37Z-implement

- **Files:** new `src/console/action.rs`; modified `src/console/keys.rs`, `src/console/mod.rs`, `src/console/view.rs`, `src/human/console.rs`, `src/human/fleet.rs`, `src/human.rs` (re-exports, companion), `src/cmd/console.rs`, `crates/viola-core/src/obs.rs`, `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`, `schemas/diag-detail.v1.json`, `tests/contract_diag_schema.rs`, `tests/tui_console.rs` (basis: `gate.py scope` — changed 13 · listed 12 · recorded 1).

- **Symbols / APIs:** (all `pub(crate)` in the root bin; no IPC method, endpoint, socket, port or env var added)
  - `console::action` (new): `Verb` {`Last`, `Pause`, `Release`, `Focus`, `Up`} with `word()` (the CLI verb and the `console-action` word) and `label()` (`revive` for `Up`, else the word); `Action { verb, name, args, stdin }` + `Action::on`; `Outcome { verb, name, exit_code, lines }`; `Runner::new(exe, home)`, `Runner::command` (`<exe> --home <home> <verb> <name> <args…>`, `VIOLA_NAME` / `VIOLA_DIR` removed through `STRIPPED`, stdin null or piped, stdout/stderr piped, no shell), `Runner::spawn` (one thread, outcome on an `mpsc` channel); `lines_of` (LF split, each line through `escape_row`). Each stream read on its own thread by `(&mut stream).take(MAX_FRAME).read_to_end(…)`, the rest past the cap drained to `io::sink`. A spawn failure or a signal end reads exit `-1`.
  - `console::keys`: `Key::of` and the scaffold's one-class-per-read `Key` {Quit, Interrupt, Unbound} retired; new `Key` {`Interrupt`, `Up`, `Down`, `Enter`, `Escape`, `Backspace`, `Char(char)`, `Unbound`}, `Decoder` (`feed(read, now)`, `deadline()`, `flush(now)`), `ESC_WAIT` 50 ms, a CSI read whole to its final byte (given up as `Unbound` at 32 bytes), SS3, one whole UTF-8 scalar across reads (C1 and malformed → `Unbound`). `spawn` now sends each read's bytes (`KeyRead = io::Result<Option<Vec<u8>>>`), `READ_CAP` 64 kept. Sole product caller of `keys::spawn`: `console::run`.
  - `console::view`: `View::of(lines, size, selected, result, keys)` (was `View::of(lines, size)`), `View::keys()`, `Selection` (`name()`, `follow`, `moved`), `wrapped_names`; the above line `... <n> above`; result rows at most a third of the body (`... <n> more` past them), laid in the body's lowest rows. Sole caller: `console::State::view`.
  - `console` (mod.rs): `Sources` gains a fourth parameter `act: A` (`FnMut(Action) -> Receiver<Outcome>`); private `Mode` {List, Confirm(Action)}, `Shown`, `State` (`view`, `press`, `reap`). `run`'s sole product caller stays `src/cmd/console.rs`.
  - `human`: `CONSOLE_KEYS` now `q quit  jk move  l last  p pause  r release  f focus  v revive`; new `console_confirm_prompt` (`<verb> <name>? y/n`), `console_running_line` (`<verb>  <name>  running`), `write_console_frame(out, rows, body, keys)` (gains `keys`); `FleetLine` gains `name: Option<String>` (a wrapped row's board item name); new `gutter`, `SELECTED_GUTTER` `> `, `GUTTER` two spaces; `escape_row` newly re-exported from `human`.
  - `viola_core::obs::ObsEvent::ConsoleAction` (`console-action`), `ALL` 18 → 19.
- **Crates / modules:** added module `src/console/action.rs`; changed `viola` (root bin) and `viola-core`.
- **Dependencies:** none.

- **Schema / config:** `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`: event enum + `console-action` message arm + field arm (`verb` enum `last` · `pause` · `release` · `focus` · `up` · `send` · `switch` · `answer` · `open`, `exit_code` integer, both required); the `console-key` arm's `key` enum grows from `quit` · `interrupt` · `unbound` to those three plus `up` · `down` · `action` · `busy` · `yes` · `no` · `escape` · `enter` · `backspace` · `text` (`enter` and `text` are Part 2's and written by no Part-1 path). `schemas/diag-detail.v1.json`: event enum + `console-action`. No config key.
- **Spec-master edits:** none.

- **Retired:** the scaffold's `Key::of` (one class per read) and its `key_of_reads_one_read_as_one_class` / `key_words_are_the_closed_three` cases, replaced by the sequence decoder and its `decoder_…` cases; the console key line `q quit` alone (now the bindings line). No census row stands for them.

- **Counts / qualifiers moved:** the closed event list 18 → 19 (`ObsEvent::ALL`, `LOG_FORMAT_EVENTS` in `crates/viola-core/src/obs.rs` and in `tests/contract_diag_schema.rs`, both schemas' event enums); the `console-key` word set 3 → 13 (`schemas/diag-line.v1.json`); the console key line's text (above).
- **Dev-tool versions:** none.
- **Harness / gate surface:** none.

- **Cross-project / external claims:** inputs#I1 (the overseer's directive, `../additional/viola-overseer/phase-console-actions-directive.md`, copy), inputs#I2 (the operator's own answers F1–F7 and the overseer's technical word, `../additional/viola-overseer/relay-console-actions-forks.md`, copy), inputs#I3 (the P5 word on `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-28T13-46-51Z-phase/p5-card-1.md`: yes to plan rev 3, by the delegate overseer — PROVISIONAL). That card's `## Beyond the plan` rows, verbatim:
  - Q8 and Q9 (`founder-forks.md`, the P4 block) — his to answer. Part 2 waits on both, and so does v2-15's claim.
  - No route entry is inserted (his F2/F7: one entry).
  - adopt from the console is not owned by any entry. If he wants it, it is a new route entry on his word: its proposed
    title would be «Console adopt», placed after «Console actions».
  The implement run's own directive (the invocation): Part 1 only, stop at Part 1's end, operator away, fakes only, no window, no real claude.
- **Reverted / negative API facts:** none.
- **Insufficient fixes (written, kept, not the remedy):** none.

- **Spec claims disproved by measurement:** plan step 9 names `console_refused_action_logs_the_verbs_exit_code` as «pause on a dead instance gives exit 21»; a dead (gone) instance draws no row to select (`crates/viola-state/src/board.rs:113` «a gone instance has no row»; `tests/tui_console.rs::console_draws_a_booted_wrapper_and_its_end` reads shown 1 → 0 at the stop). The case is built over a wrapper frozen until its heartbeat is stale, which `viola pause` refuses `instance-dead`, exit 21.

- **Expected amendments (from plan):**
  - design-system §Surface: cli (decision/list-is-the-board) — the console acts on the selected strip through the verbs: carried (**Symbols / APIs**, `console::action`), Part 1's five verbs.
  - layout-templates §Surface: cli (decision/board-vs-strip) — the same: carried.
  - security-plan §Input Validation + decision/console-runs-verbs-as-children: carried (`Runner::command`, `drain`, one at a time through `State::running`).
  - security-plan §Data Protection + decision/console-action-child-outlives-quit: carried (no parent-death tie; a running child's outcome is dropped at a quit).
  - design-system §Surface: console (contract/fleet-console-keys/unbound) and the bound keys and confirm prompts: carried for Part 1 (`jk` and the arrows, `l` `p` `f` `r` `v`, `y`/`n`/escape); Part 2's `s` `m` `a` `o` read `unbound`.
  - design-system §Surface: console + contract/fleet-console-keys/answer and /open: not carried — Part 2.
  - design-system §Surface: console (contract/fleet-console-view/more-line) + /above-line: carried (`View::of`, `... <n> above`).
  - a11y-plan §5 (decision/cli-no-interactive-input, decision/cli-not-keyboard-interactive, decision/static-linear-output): carried for the selection redraw and the confirm; the editing line is Part 2's.
  - obs-plan §1 (decision/no-interactive-terminal-interface): the same as the a11y line.
  - layout-templates §Surface: console (decision/console-frame-floor) — the key line keeps `q quit` first, then the bindings: carried (`CONSOLE_KEYS`).
  - layout-templates §Surface: console (decision/console-own-surface) — the editing echo, only on Q9 arm 1: not carried — Part 2, Q9 owed.
  - architecture §Standard Contracts + security-plan §Input Validation, only on Q8 arm 1: not carried — Part 2, Q8 owed.
  - security-plan §Input Validation (decision/console-key-reader-bounded) — the decoder's closed classes and the 50 ms lone-ESC wait, the 64-byte bound kept: carried (`Decoder`, `ESC_WAIT`, `READ_CAP`).
  - obs-plan §6 (contract/diag-line-fields/console-key) + contract/diag-line-fields/console-action, an obs Decisions Log entry: carried (**Schema / config**).
  - test-plan §3 (decision/harness-log-fields-owned-by-test-plan) — the console-action line among the grepped fields: carried (the event and its two fields).
  - matrix#v2-31 note: not this chunk's to write (P5 step 4's).

- **Coverage of new surfaces:**
  - `the console's key reader (stdin, raw)` → validation READ_CAP 64 a read + closed `Key` classes + CSI cap 32✓ · instrumentation `console-key` per key (a closed word)✓ · PII no key byte in any line✓ · tests unit (`decoder_…`) + e2e (`tui_console`) · a11y kbd: every Part-1 mode left by one key (`n`/escape from a confirm), Ctrl-C ends every mode✓ · tokens n/a
  - `an action child's stdout/stderr` → validation `take(MAX_FRAME)` per stream + `escape_row` per line✓ · instrumentation one `console-action{verb, exit_code}` per finished child✓ · PII no name, argument or output in any line✓ · tests unit (`action_…`) + e2e · a11y n/a · tokens n/a
  - `the action child's spawn (own exe, --home, VIOLA_NAME/VIOLA_DIR removed, no shell)` → validation `Runner::command`✓ · instrumentation the child's own `cli-<name>` log, as at a shell✓ · PII n/a · tests unit (`action_child_env_drops_the_instance_names`) + e2e · a11y n/a · tokens n/a
  - `the selection, the scroll, the result rows, the confirm prompt on the key row` → validation n/a · instrumentation `console-frame` shown/hidden✓ · PII n/a · tests unit (`selection_…`, `scroll_…`) + e2e · a11y kbd✓ (no key trap) · tokens n/a (plain ASCII, no colour)

- **Decoder classes:** `q`, `j` and `k` decode as `Key::Char`; the list mode gives them their meaning (quit, down, up). The plan's class list names them as decoder classes; decoded as chars, Part 2's editing line can type them as text (plan step 10: «`q` and the verb letters are text here») with no second decoder.

- **The handover (step 8):** `src/cmd/console.rs` reads the canonical exe and the canonical home once (the home after the log made it, as `plugin.rs` does) and hands the loop an action starter, `Sources.act`, built from `Runner::new(exe, home)`, rather than the two paths themselves, so the loop's unit cases inject a starter and spawn nothing.
- **Revive's word:** the action line logs `up`, the CLI verb run; the running line and the confirm read `revive`, the human's word.

- **The gutter:** every fleet line (the caption, the empty-board line and the separator included) takes the two-column gutter, so the columns stay aligned; the above, more and result lines take none. At 80 columns a row's tail is cut two columns sooner; one existing unit case (`console_run_logs_a_frame_only_when_its_fields_change`) is widened to 100 columns so its LAST tick still changes the frame, and the scaffold's frame literals in `src/console/mod.rs` and `src/human/console.rs` carry the gutter and the bindings line.
- **Busy and no selection:** an action letter while a child runs reads `busy` and opens no confirm (`r` / `v` too); a letter with no selection reads `unbound` and runs nothing.
- **Plan step 9's refused case:** a frozen (stale) wrapper in place of a dead one — **Spec claims disproved**.

- **Plan step 9's scroll case:** run at 80x5, below the floor: a body that scrolls at 80x24 needs 22+ live wrapped rows; below the floor each `console-frame` still counts the rows the body would draw, so three booted wrappers read (1,2) → (2,1) → (1,2).

data.head: ### Part 2 — the editing line, send, switch, open and answer (implement re-enters here)

body:
11. **One `console-key` line per read in the editing mode** (`src/console/mod.rs`, `run` lines 369-373 and `press`;
    inputs#I5 item 3). `run` hands `State` the whole read's keys. In the list, confirm and answer modes each key
    writes its own line, as now. In the editing mode the read's keys are folded by class: at most one `text` line
    whose `count` is the scalars appended, one `backspace` line whose `count` is the scalars removed, one `unbound`
    line whose `count` is the keys dropped (each written only when its count is at least 1), then one line for the
    `enter`, `escape` or `interrupt` that ended the read. A read writes at most four lines, whatever its length; a
    key read before `s`, `m` or `o` opened the line in the same read keeps its own line.
    - `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`, the `console-key` arm (line 99): `count` (`$ref` `#/$defs/count`, the existing def
      at line 129) beside `key`; `key` gains `question` (step 15); and a `key` of `text` requires `count`.
    - `crates/viola-core/src/obs.rs` line 12, the event list's doc: `console-key` (`key`, and `count` on an editing
      read's `text`, `backspace` and `unbound` lines).
    - `schemas/diag-detail.v1.json` holds no per-event field arm (event enum, line 14), and `tests/contract_diag_schema.rs`
      pins the event list only (line 37): neither moves. The obs-plan row
      `contract/diag-line-fields/console-key` goes to the wrap (Implementation notes).
    No line carries a typed scalar, the text, a name or a count of anything but keys.

12. **The echo and its width rule** (`src/human/console.rs`, `Cargo.toml`). New `console_editing_line(prompt, text,
    columns)`: the prompt, then the text as typed, each scalar through the board's row escape (the decoder admits no
    control, so the escape changes nothing it was handed), fitted to `columns` by one width rule —
    `unicode-width` `=0.2.2` (`UnicodeWidthChar::width`), the crate and version `vt100` already brings into
    `Cargo.lock` (line 1710; `cargo tree -i unicode-width` reads it under `vt100 v0.16.2` alone), added to
    `[workspace.dependencies]` (`Cargo.toml` line 199) and the root bin; no crate is added to the lock. The rule:
    - a scalar of width 1 takes one column: a Cyrillic line `привет` draws as typed in 6 columns, and its 12 UTF-8
      bytes reach `viola send` as typed;
    - an East Asian wide or fullwidth scalar takes two: `漢字` draws in 4 columns;
    - a combining mark (and any scalar of width 0) takes none and draws on the scalar before it: `e` + U+0301 draws as
      one column; Backspace removes the mark alone (one scalar a press);
    - when prompt and text pass `columns`, the echo is the prompt, then `...`, then the longest tail of the text that
      fits; a wide scalar that would straddle the cut is left out whole (the tail may stand one column short), and a
      width-0 scalar at the tail's head is left out with it. The whole text is still sent;
    - an invalid byte sequence never reaches the text: the decoder reads it `Unbound` (step 1), so nothing of it is
      drawn and nothing sent; it counts in the read's `unbound` line;
    - `View::of` takes the editing line as fitted: its key-line cut (`src/console/view.rs`, `cut_line` by
      `chars().count()`, `src/human/fleet.rs:136`) is not applied to it, and every other line keeps the board's cut
      unchanged (the view's content does not move, directive item 1).
    Unit cases `editing_width_…` in `src/human/console.rs`, an rstest table (keeps tests S3): Cyrillic, CJK, a combining
    mark, a wide scalar at the cut, a text past the right edge, an ASCII text equal to the old cut.

13. **send** (`src/console/action.rs`, `src/console/mod.rs`). `Verb::Send` (`send`); `s` on a selected row opens the
    editing line, its prompt `send <name>: `; Enter runs `viola send <name>` with the text on its stdin (`Action.stdin`,
    `Runner::command`'s piped stdin). Its mirror lines (`[RB] read back` · `[  ] unconfirmable` · `[/ ] unable …` and its
    hint) are its readback, drawn as captured (carry cry-qjw64paz: never STATUS). An empty line is the verb's own
    `empty-text` refusal, exit 13.

14. **switch and open a child** (`src/console/action.rs`, `src/console/mod.rs`).
    - `Verb::Switch` (`switch`): `m`, the prompt `switch <name>: `. The text is split on spaces; each word that
      `viola_agent_claude::is_effort_level` accepts (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs:173`) becomes the one
      element `--effort=<word>`, any other word `--model=<word>`. The `=` form keeps a typed word a value, never a
      flag: `parse_model` and `parse_effort` (`src/cmd/run.rs:87-101`) refuse what they refuse, exit 2.
    - `Verb::Open` (`open`): `o`, the prompt `open child of <name>: `; Enter runs `viola open <typed> --parent <name>
      -- claude`, the typed text ONE argv element. A flag-shaped text (`--home=…`, `--cwd …`) leaves `open`'s required
      name missing, so clap's own usage error, exit 2 (`OpenArgs`, `src/cmd/open.rs:41-69`; `--home` is global,
      `src/cmd/mod.rs:59`); everything else stays open's default (model, effort, workspace, cwd: the console's own).
    Each verb's line or refusal is drawn as captured.

15. **answer** (`src/console/action.rs`, `src/console/mod.rs`, `src/human/console.rs`, `crates/viola-state/src/board.rs`).
    - The board item gains `dialog_id: Option<u64>`, `#[serde(skip)]` as `dialog_kind` is (`board.rs:208-209`), read
      from the snapshot's `pending_dialog.dialog_id` in `snapshot_item` (line 384's neighbour) and `None` in
      `replayed_item` (line 412) and the unwrapped item (line 237). `list`, `list --json` and the MCP list item stay
      byte-identical. `FleetLine` carries the selected row's kind and id to the loop beside its name.
    - The console reads the kind from the board's `dialog_kind`, the snapshot's word: `permission`, `plan` or
      `question` (`crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs:109-112`).
    - `a` on a row whose dialog is a permission enters `Mode::Answer`, its prompt `answer <name> permission? y allow
      n deny`; on a plan, `answer <name> plan? y approve  n revise`. `y` / `n` runs `viola answer <name> <dialog_id>` with
      `{"behavior":"allow"}` / `{"behavior":"deny"}` or `{"behavior":"approve"}` / `{"behavior":"revise"}` on its stdin —
      the shapes `Response::parse` reads (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/dialog.rs:220-255`), no `message`. Escape
      cancels and answers nothing; Interrupt ends the console; any other key is `unbound` and stays.
    - `a` on a question draws one result line, `<name>  question - answer it in the session (f)`, writes the key word
      `question`, and starts no child (no `console-action` line). `f` then focuses it (step 6).
    - `a` on a row with no pending dialog, or a kind none of the three, is `unbound`.
    - No question, option, plan or tool text is read: the console reads the board's kind word and id alone, never the
      instance's `events.ndjson` (architecture `decision/option-text-never-in-human-line` and security-plan
      `decision/question-option-text-crosses-boundary` unmoved, his Q8). A dialog answered meanwhile is `viola answer`'s
      own refusal, drawn as captured.

16. **The key line** (`src/human/console.rs`, `CONSOLE_KEYS`): `q quit  jk move  l last  p pause  r release  f focus  v
    revive  s send  m switch  a answer  o open`, `q quit` first so a cut never hides it.

17. **Part 2's cases.**
    - Units: `editing_…` in `src/console/mod.rs` (the editing keys, the per-read fold — a 64-byte read of text writes
      one `text` line of count 64 —, the CR that ends a read, the bound); `action_send_…`, `action_switch_…` (the `=`
      form), `action_open_…`, `action_answer_…` (the four response bodies) in `src/console/action.rs`; `editing_width_…`
      (step 12); `board_read_takes_a_pending_dialog_and_its_kind` (`board.rs:958`) also asserts the id.
    - `tests/tui_console.rs`, every case under the Part-1 conditions (an outer PTY, a test-owned home and HOME, the
      test-scoped PATH, fake-agent instances only, the tied builder, verdicts from `console.ndjson`, the instance's
      `events.ndjson` and the fakes' receipts, never the screen):
      - `console_send_hands_the_line_to_the_verb_and_logs_its_exit` — the events log holds the verb's `send-issued` and
        `prompt-submitted`, and `console-action{verb:send, exit_code:0}`
      - `console_send_empty_line_is_the_verbs_refusal` — exit 13
      - `console_send_a_cyrillic_line_as_typed` — exit 0: the verb's read-back confirms the submitted text equals the
        typed text (`send.rs`)
      - `console_editing_line_left_by_escape_runs_nothing`
      - `console_editing_line_logs_one_text_line_per_read` — a paste of 200 ASCII bytes in one write: the `text` lines'
        counts sum to 200, and there are at most ⌈200 / 64⌉ of them
      - `console_switch_hands_its_words_to_the_verb` — the fake agent's start receipt carries the pair
      - `console_switch_bad_word_is_the_verbs_refusal` — exit 2
      - `console_open_hands_the_name_and_parent_to_the_verb` — the fake foot's spawn record
      - `console_answer_permission_by_y` — a permission raised through the hook (`fixtures/fake-scripts/path4-permission.json`,
        as `tests/cli_answer.rs` raises it): `dialog-answered`, `console-action{verb:answer, exit_code:0}`
      - `console_answer_plan_by_n` — a plan raised the same way: `dialog-answered` with `revise`
      - `console_answer_question_draws_one_line_and_runs_nothing` — the key word `question`, no `console-action`, no
        `dialog-answered`, and no line of `console.ndjson` holds the question's or an option's text
      - `console_answer_left_by_escape_answers_nothing`
    - `console_ctrl_c_ends_from_every_mode` (line 711) gains the editing and answer modes.
    - Fixed copy pinned by literal: the four prompts, the question line and the key line (a11y S3, tests S4).
- `src/console/action.rs` — the action table, the child spawn, the captured result (Part 1, built; Part 2 adds four verbs)
- `src/console/keys.rs` — the sequence decoder in place of `Key::of` (Part 1, built)
- `src/console/mod.rs` — the modes, the selection, the runner's channel, the ESC deadline; Part 2 the editing and answer modes and the per-read fold
- `src/console/view.rs` — the selection mark, the scroll, the above line, the result rows; Part 2 the fitted editing line
- `src/human/console.rs` — the key line, the prompts, the running line; Part 2 the editing echo and its width rule
- `src/human/fleet.rs` — the selection gutter; Part 2 the selected row's dialog kind and id on `FleetLine`
- `src/human.rs` — the re-exports of the console writers (companion of `src/human/fleet.rs` and `src/human/console.rs`)
- `src/cmd/console.rs` — the exe and home handed to the loop (Part 1, built)
- `crates/viola-core/src/obs.rs` — `ObsEvent::ConsoleAction`; Part 2 the `console-key` count in the event doc
- `crates/viola-state/src/board.rs` — Part 2: the dialog id on the item, kept out of `list --json`
- `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` — the console-action arms and the console-key words; Part 2 `count` and `question`
- `schemas/diag-detail.v1.json` — the event enum (Part 1, built)
- `tests/contract_diag_schema.rs` — the pinned event list (Part 1, built)
- `Cargo.toml` — Part 2: `unicode-width = "=0.2.2"` in `[workspace.dependencies]` and the root bin's dependencies
- `Cargo.lock` — Part 2: the root package's dependency list gains `unicode-width` (no crate added)

The block runs, in order: the formatter and the linter; the core and state crates' units; the root binaries' units and
the new unit cases of each part; the console binary whole and each part's new cases; the contract binaries the event
touches; the list binaries; the two schema arms; the supply-chain check; the host read; the harness's unit,
integration and e2e layers; then the operator pass. Each entry's `note` names its part. Part 1's entries are green on
the tree as the stopped run left it; Part 2's new-case entries read 0 cases there.

**What is not run, and why:** no round, no live entry, no live start, no real `claude`, no compositor call and no
mutation run (inputs#I1). **Boot path:** test-plan declares no boot-path list. By shape, `src/main.rs` and the run
start are untouched; Part 2 touches the board read under `viola list` (`crates/viola-state/src/board.rs`), so
`binary(cli_list) | binary(cross_list_rows)` stands as its entry. A dependency edge moves (`unicode-width`, step 12), so
`cargo deny check` stands as an entry beside CI's job.

**The remove-the-guard controls** are implement's one-shot `gate.py control` runs, never entries. Each runs on its
filtered entry below with `--timeout 900`, a clone build of the root crate and one case. Each case fails on its own
assertion with no wait, so a `timeout` reading would NOT read the guard as held. Part 1's four were run and hold
(`.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-28-console-actions/evidence/control-1.txt`); Part 2 adds two.
| `env-strip` | `src/console/action.rs` | the removal of `VIOLA_NAME` and `VIOLA_DIR` from the child's env | `action_child_env_drops_the_instance_names` | the part-1 unit filter (run, holds) |
| `one-child` | `src/console/mod.rs` | the running-child check before an action starts | `console_run_takes_one_action_at_a_time` | the part-1 unit filter (run, holds) |
| `confirm` | `src/console/mod.rs` | the confirm mode before release (it runs at once) | `console_release_confirm_left_by_escape_runs_nothing` | the part-1 e2e filter (run, holds) |
| `out-escape` | `src/console/action.rs` | the escape of a captured line (the line raw) | `action_output_escapes_every_control` | the part-1 unit filter (run, holds) |
| `text-fold` | `src/console/mod.rs` | the editing mode's per-read fold (each char its own `text` line) | `editing_a_read_of_text_writes_one_text_line` | the part-2 unit filter |
| `flag-value` | `src/console/action.rs` | the `=` form of a switch word (`--model` and the word as two elements) | `action_switch_words_are_values_never_flags` | the part-2 unit filter |

body:
- (security) An action runs its verb as a direct child of the console's own exe, `--home` passed, with `VIOLA_NAME` and
  `VIOLA_DIR` absent from its env, no shell, and its output read through `MAX_FRAME`:
  `action_child_env_drops_the_instance_names` and `contract_bounded_readers` green (F1, inputs#I2; arch
  `decision/no-shell-out`). Met by Part 1; held by Part 2.

- (product) From a selected wrapped row, by keyboard alone, `l` `p` `f` run last, pause and focus, and `r`·`y` and
  `v`·`y` run release and `up <name>`. Each gives the verb's own record and exit, equal to the shell verb's, and one
  `console-action{verb, exit_code}` line: the part-1 e2e filter green. Met by Part 1.

- (product) `s` sends the editing line through `viola send` and draws its mirror lines as its readback; `m` switches
  through `viola switch`; `o` opens a child through `viola open --parent`: the part-2 e2e filter green.

- (product, his Q8) `a` answers a pending permission (`y` allow / `n` deny) and a pending plan (`y` approve / `n`
  revise) through `viola answer`, and on a question draws one line naming the session and starts no child, no question
  or option text reaching the screen or any line: `console_answer_permission_by_y`, `console_answer_plan_by_n`,
  `console_answer_question_draws_one_line_and_runs_nothing` green.

- (layout, his Q9) The editing line echoes the text as typed under the width rule — Cyrillic, CJK, a combining mark, a
  wide scalar at the cut, a text past the right edge — and the text sent is unchanged: the `editing_width_…` cases and
  `console_send_a_cyrillic_line_as_typed` green.

- (obs) The editing line writes one `console-key` line per read with the class `text` and a count, never a line per
  character, and the `console-key` arm names `count`: `editing_a_read_of_text_writes_one_text_line`,
  `console_editing_line_logs_one_text_line_per_read` green; the console-key probe reads `count,key`. `console-action`
  is in `ObsEvent::ALL`, both schemas' event enums and both pinned lists, and the console-action probe reads
  `verb,exit_code` (met by Part 1).

- (a11y) No key trap: every mode is left by one key (`n` or escape from a confirm, escape from the editing line and from
  an answer), and Ctrl-C ends the console from every mode, exit 0 and the line mode cooked after (test-plan
  `decision/console-restore-read-on-own-terminal`): `console_ctrl_c_ends_from_every_mode`,
  `console_release_confirm_left_by_escape_runs_nothing`, `console_editing_line_left_by_escape_runs_nothing` and
  `console_answer_left_by_escape_answers_nothing` green.

- (security) The decoder reads at most 64 bytes a read, decodes a sequence split across reads as one key, and writes no
  key byte to any line: the part-1 unit filter green (security-plan `decision/console-key-reader-bounded`). Met by
  Part 1.

- (layout) The selection survives a fleet change by name, and the body follows it with `... <n> above` and
  `... <n> more`: `console_selection_keeps_its_name_when_the_fleet_changes` and `console_scroll_follows_the_selection`
  green (F3, F6). Met by Part 1.
- (tests) the unit, integration and e2e layers of `scripts/agent-run.sh` return `"ok":true` at each part's end.

- (matrix) matrix#v2-15 — GATED, its answer leg narrowed by his dated note (permissions and plans, not questions;
  inputs#I5): the eight verbs and switch are proven over the fakes by the part-1 and part-2 e2e filters; its live half —
  on his Hyprland host, against his real `claude` and terminal, each action from a selected row (focus raising his
  window, open and revive opening their terminals, send's readback, answer on a real permission and plan, switch's
  restart, the echo drawn by his terminal) — waits on his live reading at a moment he names (inputs#I1), and no
  stand-in verifies it. gated: BLOCKED-ON: the operator's live reading of viola console's actions on his Hyprland host — open a child, focus, send, answer (a permission and a plan), last, pause, release, revive and switch from a selected row, against his real claude and terminal — at a moment he names (chunks/2026-11-28-console-actions/inputs/I1-phase-console-actions-directive.md.txt)

- The operator's answers and the overseer's technical word: inputs#I2 (F1–F7), inputs#I5 (Q8, Q9 and the revision's
  six orders); the stop: inputs#I4; the directive: inputs#I1; the forks as priced:
  `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-28T13-46-51Z-phase/founder-forks.md` (the P4 block).

- Research files inspected: the take-up's list, and at this revision `src/console/action.rs`, `src/console/mod.rs`,
  `src/console/keys.rs`, `src/console/view.rs`, `src/human/console.rs`, `src/human/fleet.rs`,
  `crates/viola-state/src/board.rs`, `crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs`, `src/cmd/answer.rs`, `src/cmd/open.rs`,
  `src/cmd/switch.rs`, `src/cmd/run.rs`, `src/cmd/mod.rs`, `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`.

- Colour or reverse video for the selection — the console is plain ASCII with no colour
  (layout-templates `decision/console-own-surface`); the editing line alone is excepted, by his Q9.

- A question answered from the console (Q8 arm 1) — his answer leaves it to the session; the console reads no
  question or option text.

- A width table written in viola's own code — a second rule beside the one `vt100` already places cells by; the crate
  in the lock is reused instead.
- A line per typed char in the editing mode — inputs#I5 item 3; a paste would write one line a byte.
- The switch word as two argv elements (`--model`, word) — a typed `--home …` would read as a flag.

- **Re-entry.** Steps 1–9 stand built and green (the outcome file); implement starts at step 10 and re-runs every
  entry at the end, Part 1's included. Part 1's controls are not re-run (evidence/control-1.txt); Part 2's two are.

- **Log volume per hour.** No loop or timer that writes is added; every line is independent of the fleet's size
  (33 instances or one):
  - `console-key`: one line a key read in the list, confirm and answer modes; at most four a read in the editing mode,
    whatever its length. A human's keystroke arrives as its own read, so steady typing writes about one line a key —
    at 5 keys a second, 18 000 lines in an hour of unbroken typing, about 2.9 MB at about 160 B a line (estimated from
    the line's fields, not measured). A paste of 10 KiB is at least 160 reads of 64 bytes: at most 640 lines, no
    longer 10 240.
  - `console-action`: one line a finished child, one child at a time, bounded by the human's keys; a question's line
    writes none.
  - The decoder's ESC wait, the runner's two reader threads and the child's wait write nothing.
  - Each child verb writes its own `cli-<name>.ndjson` lines, as at a shell.
  - The agents thread's 720 pairs an hour stand unchanged (obs-plan `decision/console-agents-probe-volume`).
