- cli: no interactive prompt, pager or redraw, and input is stdin / `--file` only, except the terminal fleet console (`viola console`), its own surface, which reads keys from stdin in raw mode, its one editing line, for send, switch and open, taking one line echoed as typed (Enter hands it to the verb, Escape cancels and runs nothing), and redraws on a resize, a change in the fleet it shows or a key that moves its selection or opens a prompt; tui: once the child starts the terminal belongs to the child, and viola writes zero bytes of its own to it (only a start's automatic verify lines L1 to L5 and verify's own output precede the child's bytes, and only a not-resumed `viola adopt`'s refusal pair or document follows them once the child ends) (under `viola revive --json` or `viola adopt --json` a `pump_child` error prints no document: viola writes nothing past it, and a peer the wrapper refuses is dropped in `accept_loop`, before its worker thread and any frame: it writes nothing to the outer terminal and moves no wheel), and once the wrapped child holds the terminal, human keystrokes are never blocked, refused or dropped: queued with the paste in arrival order, they wait behind at most its in-flight chunk and closing marker (the one exception is a start's automatic verify window, before the child starts: a key typed then waits in the terminal's own buffer), and focus / mouse / resize sequences and terminal replies (F-W2's closed list) are never counted as editing; every other byte is. viola has no web or graphical frontend; the terminal fleet console's keyboard reach is the route entry «Fleet a11y verification»'s, and it has no key trap: n or Escape leaves a confirm, Escape leaves the editing line and the answer prompt running nothing, and Ctrl-C ends the console from every mode with the terminal restored.

- On the CLI, state is always a printed word (`stale`, `DIALOG <kind>`, `expired`, `unverified-cli`, the STATUS words `idle` / `busy` on joined wrapped rows and the unwrapped rows' `n/a` cells; on a terminal too narrow only an unwrapped NAME is cut, to the column less 3 characters plus `...` and never inside a `\xHH` escape, a wrapped NAME never, and piped output and `--json` keep every name whole); colour is a second cue only (amber SGR only on `DIALOG`, dim on stale rows, bold only on NAME values, always beside the word), `unable` / `fail` are never coloured, and viola emits no SGR of its own under non-TTY / `NO_COLOR` (an empty value included) / `TERM=dumb` / `--json` / a passthrough role / `viola run` / a passed `viola revive` / a passed `viola adopt`, and `viola link` / `viola unlink` print one plain-ASCII result line in one write with no SGR in any mode, and `viola up` prints one line per instance, `<name>  <word>` or `<name>  live  <placement>`, plain ASCII, with no SGR, each line in one write, and `viola switch` prints one line, `<name>  switched  <model> <effort>`, on stdout in plain ASCII with no SGR. The fleet console's selection is carried by a gutter mark on the selected row alone, never by colour. viola has no web or graphical frontend, so no page token pair or layout to verify.

viola-core, viola-pty, viola-agent-claude, viola-state, viola-channel and viola-mcp (not every workspace member: viola-hyprland only as a dev-dependency); clap, anyhow, tracing-subscriber, chrono (direct, for `MillisUtc`), libc `=0.2.189` (`backtrace` + `dladdr` for the raw, never-symbolised panic frames of `src/panic_frames.rs`, and `sigaction` for `src/cmd/verify/stop.rs`'s `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM` handler, `SA_RESTART`; neither role added a dependency or a feature; no crate depends on windows-sys); tempfile (`=3.27.0`, workspace-pinned: `viola verify`'s Run A temp dir only); unicode-width (direct, exactly pinned: the terminal column widths of the console's editing line; already in the lock through vt100).

Path-scoped rules for viola's built design surfaces, human CLI output (cli) and the terminal fleet console (console); viola renders no page and has no web-spa surface; the keyboard-driven terminal fleet console tiled on Hyprland (matrix#v2-14), `viola console`, is its own surface in the human's terminal, entered on the alternate screen with the cursor hidden and restored on every end, in plain ASCII with no colour bar the editing line of send, switch and open, which echoes its text as typed (UTF-8 included) through row escaping, each scalar 1, 2 or 0 columns wide, re-reading the board once a second and redrawing only when its view changes; its frame floor is 80x24 (at or above it the whole frame from a cleared top-left, `viola console` on row 1 and the key line on the last row; below it one line `viola console needs 80x24; this terminal is <cols>x<rows>`, an unread size counting as 0x0; a line wider than the terminal is cut whole at its columns ending in `...`, never inside an escape, an unwrapped NAME not cut separately, and a fleet taller than the body rows, its scroll window not at the fleet's end, ends in `... <n> more` and one scrolled past its top begins with `... <n> above`), and `q`, Ctrl-C or the end of its input end it with exit 0 from every mode; j, k and the arrows move the selection over wrapped rows, and l last, p pause, r release, f focus, v revive (`viola up`), s send, m switch, a answer and o open each run on the selected row as its CLI verb in a child, one at a time (a static running line standing meanwhile, the verb's own escaped output its result rows), every key bound to nothing in its mode ignored; it draws the fleet as body lines between its title line and its key line, the board's rows in the board's forest order and indent. Authoritative sources: `.andromeda/design-system.md` and `.andromeda/layout-templates.md`.

- viola has no web or graphical frontend; its view beyond `viola list` is the keyboard-driven terminal fleet console tiled on Hyprland (matrix#v2-14), opened by `viola console` (no `--json`; it reads the human's keys from its own terminal in raw mode in reads of at most 64 bytes, each read decoded into keys of closed classes, an escape sequence bounded in its wait and its length, no key byte reaching any log line; its codes-only log `diagnostics/console.ndjson`; every action a child of its own executable with `--home`, the verb and the name, `VIOLA_NAME` and `VIOLA_DIR` removed, never through a shell and one child at a time, each output stream read under `MAX_FRAME` and each line escaped before it is drawn), whose remaining contracts are owed by the 0.2.0 route entry «Console scaffold». There is no `ui` subcommand and no listening TCP port; the MCP server is stdio only.

- `viola adopt` is refused like `run` when the name is `live` or `stale`, and with `session-live`, exit 1, when a `claude agents --json` row carries the id (a failed read passes); a refusal, or a resumed child ending before its session starts (`not-resumed`, its document printed after the child released the terminal), exits 1, under `--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` document (`strict-modes-failed` · `session-live` · `not-resumed` · `already-live` · `stale-heartbeat` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `squatted-name` · `socket-dir-refused` · `internal-error`). `viola open <name> [--parent <name>] [--role overseer|builder|worker] [--cwd <dir>] [--workspace N] [--model M] [--effort E] [--json] -- claude` — open a session in its own terminal window (refused like `run` when the name is `live` or `stale`); exit 0 once the session went live (the human line `<name>  live  <placement>`, under `--json` `{"v":1,"ok":{"name","parent","window","placement"}}`, window `{address, workspace}` or null), 1 for a refusal (`strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `stale-heartbeat` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `terminal-not-found` · `not-live` · `internal-error`, under `--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` document), 2 for a usage error (a clap error, any word after `--` but `claude` alone, or a parent equal to the opened name). `viola focus <name> [--json]` — raise the named session's window (takes one ViolaName and `--json` only; CLI only, no MCP tool raises a window); exit 1 with one process-exit detail: `window-not-found` (no window of the session, nothing dispatched), `unsupported` (no hyprctl reachable, nothing spawned), `unreachable` (hyprctl reachable, no compositor answering) or the hyprctl seam's `oversize`, `malformed` or `refused`; exit 21 on a refused strict-modes check (under `--json` `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}`, nothing opened, no line written). `viola up [<NAME>...] [--dry-run] [--json]` — after a reboot, re-open each instance gone before the boot through `viola revive` in a new terminal, parents before children (a live or stale instance skipped; an unnamed one ended on purpose stays down; names given narrow the fleet, a name not scanned reads `not-taken`; `--dry-run` spawns nothing; CLI only, no MCP tool); exit 0 when every line reads `live`, `already-live`, `stale-heartbeat` or `would-open`, 1 for any other line or a refusal (`boot-time-unread` · `strict-modes-failed` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `terminal-not-found`, under `--json` its document), 21 when its board scan's strict-modes check refuses (`instance-unreachable`, `strict-modes-failed`, no line printed). No `viola ui` subcommand: viola has no web or graphical frontend; its view beyond `viola list` is the keyboard-driven terminal fleet console tiled on Hyprland (matrix#v2-14), the verb `viola console` (no `--json`; it writes only its screen to stdout, in the alternate screen, with no colour and plain ASCII bar the editing line, which echoes the typed text as typed with every control escaped, its refusals and internal error to stderr; a home another user may read exits 1 with the home pair, writing no line at its start and one `process-exit` line of detail `strict-modes-failed` when its board scan is refused mid-run, after the terminal's restore; it logs to the home-level `diagnostics/console.ndjson` with no instance), owed by the 0.2.0 Epoch 6 route entries «Console scaffold», «Fleet console view» and «Console actions». `viola switch <name> [--model <MODEL>] [--effort <EFFORT>] [--json]` — switch a running wrapped session's model and effort in place, resuming the same session id on the new pair under the same wrapper (at least one of `--model` and `--effort`, else a usage error, exit 2; prints `<name>  switched  <model> <effort>` and exits 0, 10, 12, 13, 14, 20 or 21; CLI only, no MCP tool switches a session's model or effort). `viola mcp [--home <dir>]` — the stdio MCP server (tools `send · wait · last · answer · list`), hidden from `viola --help` and run by the plugin, never by a person: no argument but the global `--home`, it serves until stdin closes or a stdin line passes `MAX_FRAME` (refused whole, never truncated or skipped, with one `parse-rejected{parser:"mcp-stdin", detail:"oversize", count:1}` line holding no byte of it), which ends the session as a close does (exit 0 once initialized, 1 before `initialize`, both streams empty), and exits 1 with nothing on stdout or stderr and no role file when its home or `diagnostics/` fails `viola_state::strict::check_path` (that exit does not block the CLI's start: the session reaches `idle` and the CLI logs the server's connection as failed, measured on claude 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host)

- Bold only for the NAME column, SGR dim for `stale` rows, amber for the `DIALOG` word; ASCII only, high density, bar the fleet console's editing line, which echoes the typed text as typed, UTF-8 included, controls escaped. No font stacks or render assertions: viola renders no page.

- **web-spa** — no web surface: viola renders no page; the keyboard-driven terminal fleet console tiled on Hyprland (matrix#v2-14) is its own surface, `viola console`, in the human's terminal: entered on the alternate screen with the cursor hidden and restored on every end, plain ASCII, no colour, bar the editing line of send, switch and open, which echoes its text as typed (UTF-8 included, controls escaped), each scalar 1, 2 or 0 columns wide; the fleet drawn as body lines between the title line and the key line, the board's rows in the board's forest order and indent, under the board's six captions then a seventh, `LAST` (the age of the instance's newest log line in one unit, `12s`, `4m`, `2h`, `3d`; `unknown` on a wrapped row with no log line, `n/a` on an unwrapped row); a line wider than the terminal cut whole at its columns ending in `...`, never inside an escape, an unwrapped NAME not cut separately; a fleet taller than the body rows ending in `... <n> more` while its scroll window is not at the fleet's end, and beginning with `... <n> above` once the window is past its top; the board re-read once a second and redrawn only when the view changes, the claude agents list read on its own thread at most once every 5 s; frame floor 80x24 (`viola console` on row 1, the key line on the last row; below it the one line `viola console needs 80x24; this terminal is <cols>x<rows>`); `q`, Ctrl-C (from every mode) or end of input end it with exit 0; j, k and the arrows move the selection (marked by its gutter, over wrapped rows only), and l last, p pause, r release, f focus, v revive (`viola up`), s send, m switch, a answer and o open each run on the selected row as its CLI verb in a child, one at a time (release and revive after a `y` confirm; s, m and o through one editing line; a static running line while a child runs, other action keys reading busy; the child's escaped output lines the result rows); every key bound to nothing in its mode ignored

- **CLI** — `viola list` (the k9s-style board, six fixed columns and words the terminal fleet console (matrix#v2-14) reuses, adding `LAST` after them; as built: uncoloured under `--json`, a piped stdout, `NO_COLOR` (an empty value included) or `TERM=dumb`, else NAME bold, the `DIALOG` word amber with its kind word plain and a wrapped `stale` row dim end to end; on a terminal whose width is known (`viola_pty::host_size()`, never `COLUMNS`) only an unwrapped NAME too long for its column is cut with `...`; the wrapped rows drawn as a tree, each child directly under its parent with its NAME cell indented two spaces per depth, then, when one `claude agents --json` read lists a session no wrapped row joins, the `-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --` line and one row per unwrapped session (NAME its `sessionId`, `n/a` in WHEEL, DIALOG and CLI), then, when there is a link, the `-- LINKS --` line and one `<driver> -> <driven>` line per link, sorted, deduplicated, no SGR; STATUS `idle` / `busy` on a row the read joins, else `unknown`; a failed read prints the board as with no `claude`; and a failed strict-modes check refuses the whole board with exit 21, or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document with `detail` `strict-modes-failed`), the `viola send` readback mirror (an unusable `viola send`, an oversize `viola answer` and a `--model` / `--effort` pair after the `--` of `viola run` or `viola revive` instead exit 2 with their fixed stderr line, `UNUSABLE_TEXT` / `UNUSABLE_RESPONSE` / `PAIR_AFTER_DASHES`, whatever `--json` says, and no document; a failed `cli` verb's `error: internal error`, exit 1, is with `--json` among the arguments before a `--` the document `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` on stdout with stderr empty, while `run`, `revive`'s start, `adopt`, `mcp` and `hook` stay silent at the catch site), phraseology verb output (`viola plugin install`: four plain-ASCII stdout lines in one write, no SGR, `viola@viola  written  <dir>` / `run these to add it to Claude Code:` / `  claude plugin marketplace add <dir>` / `  claude plugin install viola@viola`, `<dir>` quoted only where the host's shell would split it; under `--json` `{"v":1,"ok":{"marketplace":"viola","plugin":"viola@viola"}}`; a refused strict-modes check is exit 21 with `viola list`'s home pair on stderr, or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document with `detail` `strict-modes-failed`, stderr empty), `viola wait` / `viola last` (one static result line on stdout, no spinner; a `wait` woken by an expired dialog hold prints `dialog-expired  <name>  dialog <id>  cursor <n>`, ASCII, no SGR, written once), `viola link` / `viola unlink` (one plain-ASCII stdout line in one write, no SGR, exit 0: `link    <driver> -> <driven>  since <HH:MM:SSZ>`, `link    <driver> -> <driven>  already linked` for a held pair, `unlink  <driver> -> <driven>` whether or not a pair was removed; under `--json` `{"v":1,"ok":{"since":<ts>,"already_linked":<bool>}}` / `{"v":1,"ok":{}}`; a refused strict-modes check of the driven instance is exit 21 with `revive`'s instance pair on stderr naming it, and so is the one `viola send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release` and `switch` make of their instance before any frame (that pair, not the `[/ ]` mirror; no frame and no line written), or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document with `detail` `strict-modes-failed`, stderr empty (exit 21's document is `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"<cause>"}`, `<cause>` one of `strict-modes-failed` · `instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name` · `endpoint-lost` · `server-verify-failed` · `socket-dir-refused`)), `viola verify` step counter (a run whose first screen met claude's trust or imports form is refused before any row is read, exit 1, code `untrusted-folder`, its fixed `unable:` / `hint:` pair, no step line, no summary, no stamp; each relied row's step line ends `pass`, `absent` or `fail`, `absent` only on the `browser-tools-prompt` row when no run met the prompt, counted as a pass there alone, and a run that met that prompt prints, after a successful `stamps.json` update and before the summary, one plain ASCII stdout line, no SGR: `the browser-tools prompt stood at start; viola never answers it: answer it once in claude, then run viola verify again`; the trust-record row's ends `pass` or `fail`; no step line, summary or refusal names the config file, the trust record's key or its value), `viola open <name>` (a wrapped claude session in a new foot terminal window beside its parent; flags a closed allowlist, only `claude` after `--`, no shell runs; it prints one of eight closed placement words `placed` · `refused` · `unplaced` · `unsupported` · `window-unseen` · `unreachable` · `oversize` · `malformed`), `viola focus <name>` (brings the named session's window forward and shows its workspace on Hyprland; one name and `--json` only, a CLI-only human control; prints `<name>  focused` on stdout, or under `--json` `{"v":1,"ok":{"name":"<name>"}}`, no window address, pid or workspace ever printed or logged; a name not live or a failed strict-modes check exits 21 before any compositor read, and its exit-1 refusals are six closed codes `refused` · `unsupported` · `window-not-found` · `unreachable` · `oversize` · `malformed`), `viola console` (shows the terminal fleet console, acting on its selected strip only through the CLI verbs it runs as children; no argument, the global `--home` only, no `--json`; exit 0 on quit, interrupt or end of input, 1 on a refusal or an internal error; with stdin or stdout not a terminal, before any home read, `unable: viola console needs a terminal` / `hint: run viola console in a terminal window`; a home failing its read rule `unable: viola console could not use its home` / `hint: make the viola home readable by you alone, then run viola console again`, at its start with no line written and the mode left as found, mid-run after the terminal is restored with one process-exit line of detail `strict-modes-failed`; a board directory that cannot be listed ends it as `error: internal error`), `viola up [<NAME>...] [--dry-run] [--json]` (re-opens the fleet after a reboot, each candidate revived in its own terminal, parents before children, CLI-only; one stdout line per instance, `<name>  <word>` or `<name>  live  <placement>` with a closed placement word, the word one of nine closed outcome words, or under `--json` `{"v":1,"ok":{"instances":[{"name","outcome","placement"}]}}`), `viola adopt <SESSION_ID> --name <NAME>` (resumes a plain claude session by its session id under viola with the given name and parent, in the current folder, with no window; prints nothing once the child starts except at its not-resumed end, which after the child released the terminal exits 1 with `unable: <name>'s session did not resume` / `hint: check the session id - claude --resume <id> must open it by hand, under the same claude config` or its `--json` document, and a resumed child ends exit 0; a `pump_child` error under `--json` prints no document), `viola switch <name> [--model <MODEL>] [--effort <EFFORT>] [--json]` (switches a running wrapped session to a new model and effort in place, resuming the same session id; at least one of `--model` and `--effort` is required, else a usage error, exit 2; a success prints `<name>  switched  <model> <effort>` on stdout, exit 0, or under `--json` one stdout document whose `ok` carries the new `model` and `effort`; it exits 0, 10, 12, 13, 14, 20 or 21 and writes nothing to the user's own settings), the `viola run` / `viola revive` passthrough (on a verified CLI the start writes the claude CLI's trust record for an untrusted session folder, flag only, so no trust dialog stands and no key is typed, `revive`'s keyed by the recorded directory; the trust step adds no refusal, exit code, hint, `--json` code or terminal byte; before the child only a key-on start's automatic verify line (one stderr write, ASCII, no SGR, naming the parsed claude version and a closed word, none under `--json`) and verify's own output reach the terminal (discarded under `revive --json`); nothing printed while the child runs, nor at a switch's respawn of the child; `viola revive <name> --list` prints one static line per logged session; under `--json` both arms print one stdout document: `--list`'s `{"v":1,"ok":{"sessions":[…]}}`, every refusal of the start it shares with `run`, `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` with exit 1, no hint and stderr empty, `<code>` one of `strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing` · `stale-heartbeat` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `squatted-name` · `socket-dir-refused` · `internal-error`; a `pump_child` error prints none, the child having held the terminal; a start refusal of `viola adopt`, or its not-resumed end after the child ran, exits 1 with its fixed `unable:` / `hint:` pair, or under `--json` one stdout document `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` and no hint, stderr empty)

**Stack:** Rust 1.98.1 pinned by `rust-toolchain.toml` (edition 2024, `rust-version` 1.96), one Cargo workspace (`crates/*`, the `fuzz/` workspace excluded) building one native `viola` binary: std threads with Tokio only inside `viola-mcp`, clap `=4.6.7`, portable-pty `=0.9.0` behind viola's own PTY seam, vt100 `=0.16.2` for readiness, unicode-width (a direct, exactly pinned dependency of the root bin) for the console editing line's column widths, interprocess `=2.4.4` local sockets carrying JSON-RPC 2.0 over ndjson, ndjson append logs and atomic JSON snapshots (no database, broker, container or hosting), rmcp 3.4.1 (`>=3.4.1, <3.5`) for the stdio MCP server; CI on GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest` against the fake agent; deployed by a local `cargo install`, the plugin embedded and loaded with `--plugin-dir`.
